title: Editor layout: top bar, left dock, canvas, inspector and status bar
steps: Open the app in Chrome with a 1600x900 window.
Resize the window to 1280x800.
expected: A top bar spans the full window width at the top and shows the product name taken from src/config/product.ts; the browser tab title is the same name.
A left dock shows the Elements panel above the Layers panel, a right dock shows the Inspector, and a status bar spans the bottom.
The canvas fills the space between the two docks, between the top bar and the status bar.
At both window sizes the measured bounding boxes of top bar, left dock, canvas, inspector and status bar do not overlap, together cover the window, and the window has no page scrollbar.
The bottom workbench dock is closed by default; panels added by later entries open as tabs in existing docks or in that workbench, so these five regions stay the default layout.

title: The page renders from the document JSON inside a zoomed iframe
steps: Open the app with no saved project.
Resize the window from 1600x900 to 1280x800.
expected: The canvas holds exactly one iframe whose body renders the Page root node of the document JSON.

The canvas reserves a 20 px band along its top and left edges for rulers (empty until rulers are built); the remaining area is the canvas viewport. Inside the iframe the page is 1440 CSS px wide (the Desktop breakpoint); the iframe is scaled with CSS zoom so the whole page width fits in the canvas viewport, horizontally centred in it.
The zoom percentage in the status bar equals the iframe zoom factor and is recomputed after the resize.
An empty page shows the hint 'Click an element or drag it onto this page' [canvas.emptyHint]; the hint is not a node in the document JSON.

title: Insert Section, Container, Heading and Paragraph by clicking the Elements panel
steps: With nothing selected, click Section in the Elements panel.
Click Heading.
Click Paragraph.
Click Container.
expected: The Elements panel lists each element type with its label and HTML tag under a group heading with a count.
With nothing selected, the Section is appended as the last child of Page in the document JSON and becomes the selection.
With a container selected, the Heading is appended as its last child; with a non-container selected, the Paragraph is inserted right after it in the same parent.

Every inserted element becomes the selection; the iframe shows
,

'New heading' [element.heading.defaultText],

with default text and an empty

with a visible minimum height.
The status bar reads 'Placed <name> in <parent>, position N of M.' [status.placed] after each insert.

title: Select an element by clicking it on the canvas
steps: Insert a Section containing a Heading and a Paragraph.
Click the Paragraph on the canvas.
Click inside the Section's padding, away from its children.
Click the empty page area below the Section.
Hover the Heading without clicking.
Press Escape.
expected: After each click the document selection is the clicked element; a selection outline matches the element's measured bounding box on the canvas and a label shows its tag and name.
Clicking the Section's padding selects the Section, not a child; clicking empty page area selects the Page root.
Hovering shows a thinner hover outline around the Heading and does not change the selection.
Escape clears the selection and removes the selection outline.

title: Layers panel shows the document tree and selects in sync with the canvas
steps: Insert a Section containing a Heading and a Paragraph, then a Container after the Section.
Click the Paragraph row in the Layers panel.
Click the Container on the canvas.
Click the caret of the Section row twice.
expected: Layers shows one row per node in document order, indented by depth, with a caret on rows that have children and an icon per element type.
Clicking a row selects that element: the canvas selection outline moves to it.
Selecting on the canvas highlights the matching row and scrolls it into view.
The caret collapses and expands the branch without changing the selection.
The panel header shows the node count, and it updates after every insert.

title: Undo and redo every document change
steps: Insert three elements.
Press Ctrl+Z three times.
Press Ctrl+Shift+Z twice and Ctrl+Y once.
Undo once, then insert a new element.
Use the Undo and Redo buttons in the top bar.
expected: Each Ctrl+Z restores the document JSON to exactly its state before the matching command; Ctrl+Shift+Z and Ctrl+Y redo it.
The top bar Undo and Redo buttons do the same and are disabled when there is nothing to undo or redo.
A new command after an undo empties the redo stack (Redo becomes disabled).
After undo or redo the selection is the one that belonged to that document state.
The status bar reads 'Undone' [status.undone] or 'Redone' [status.redone].

title: Delete the selected element with Delete or Backspace
steps: Insert a Section with a Heading and two Paragraphs.
Select the first Paragraph and press Delete.
Select the Section and press Backspace.
Select the Page root and press Delete.
Press Ctrl+Z twice.
expected: Delete and Backspace remove the selected node and its whole subtree from the document JSON.
After a delete the selection moves to the next sibling, else the previous sibling, else the parent.
The Page root is never deleted; the status bar explains why.
Undo restores each deleted subtree at its original index with its original ids.

title: Drag an element before or after a sibling on the canvas
steps: Insert a Section with a Heading and two Paragraphs.
Press on the second Paragraph, drag it over the upper half of the Heading and release.
Drag the Heading over the lower half of the Paragraph that is now last and release.
Press and release on a Paragraph moving the mouse less than 4 px.
expected: While dragging, an insertion line is drawn in the gap where the element will land, the receiving parent is tinted, a chip with the element name follows the pointer, and a label reads 'Move to position N · <parent> · before <sibling>' [drag.label.before].
On release the order of children in the document JSON matches the last indicator exactly and the dragged element stays selected.
A press and release under the drag threshold only selects; the document JSON is unchanged.
Each drop is exactly one undo step.

title: Drop an element inside a container and move it across parents
steps: Insert a Section with a Heading and a Paragraph, then an empty Container after the Section.
Drag the Heading onto the empty Container and release.
Drag the Paragraph into the Container above the Heading and release.
Drag the Container onto the Paragraph inside it and release.
expected: The empty Container shows a minimum drop area, is outlined as the receiver and the label reads 'Into <container>' [drag.label.into].
The Heading becomes the Container's only child, then the Paragraph becomes its first child, in the document JSON.
Leaf elements (heading, paragraph) are never offered as receivers.
Dropping an element into itself or one of its descendants is refused: the indicator shows the refusal and release leaves the document JSON unchanged.

title: Change the drop level with arrow keys and cancel a drag with Escape
steps: Insert a Section containing a Container that contains a Paragraph, and a Heading after the Section.
Drag the Heading over the lower half of the Paragraph; without releasing press ArrowUp twice, then ArrowDown once, then release.
Start another drag of the Heading, press Escape, then release the mouse.
expected: ArrowUp moves the target out one level at a time and the status bar names it ('After Paragraph' [status.drop.after] -> 'After Container' [status.drop.after] -> 'After Section' [status.drop.after]); ArrowDown moves it back one level; the indicator and label follow.
Release drops exactly at the level last shown ('After Container' [status.drop.after] in the status bar).
Escape removes every drag indicator and the following release changes nothing in the document JSON.

title: Drag an element type from the Elements panel to a position on the canvas
steps: Insert a Section with a Heading and a Paragraph.
Drag Paragraph from the Elements panel between the Heading and the Paragraph on the canvas and release.
Drag Container from the Elements panel below the Section and release.
Drag Heading from the Elements panel onto the dark area outside the page and release.
Drag Heading onto the page and press Escape before releasing.
expected: During the drag the same insertion line, receiver tint and label as a canvas move are shown.
The new Paragraph lands at index 1 of the Section and the Container lands after the Section in the document JSON; each new element becomes selected.
Releasing outside the page or after Escape inserts nothing.
Each insert is one undo step.

title: Reorder and nest by dragging rows in the Layers panel
steps: Insert a Section with a Heading and a Paragraph, and an empty Container after it.
In Layers, drag the Paragraph row over the top quarter of the Heading row and release.
Drag the Heading row over the middle of the Container row and release.
Collapse the Section row, drag the Container row over it and hold still for 600 ms.
expected: Over the top or bottom quarter of a row a line shows 'before' or 'after'; over the middle of a container row the row is outlined for 'inside'.
Release moves the node in the document JSON to that place and the canvas updates.
Hovering a collapsed container row during a drag expands it after 600 ms.
For the same source and target, a drop in Layers and a drop on the canvas produce identical document JSON, including refusals.

title: Move the selection up or down among its siblings with Alt+ArrowUp and Alt+ArrowDown
steps: Insert a Section with a Heading and two Paragraphs.
Select the last Paragraph on the canvas and press Alt+ArrowUp twice.
Press Alt+ArrowUp again.
Press Alt+ArrowDown.
expected: Each Alt+ArrowUp swaps the element with its previous sibling in the document JSON; Alt+ArrowDown with its next sibling.

At the first or last position the document JSON is unchanged and the status bar reads 'Already at the start of <parent>' [status.move.alreadyFirst] or 'Already at the end of <parent>' [status.move.alreadyLast].
The element stays selected and each move is one undo step.

title: Wrap the selection in a Row or a Column with R and C
steps: Insert a Section with a Heading and a Paragraph.
Select the Paragraph on the canvas and press R.
Press Ctrl+Z, then press C.
Select the Page root and press R.
expected: R replaces the Paragraph at its index with a new div named 'Row' [node.name.row] whose only child is the Paragraph; the Row has display:flex and flex-direction:row in the document JSON and its computed style.
C does the same with a div named 'Column' [node.name.column] and flex-direction:column.
The new wrapper is selected; one undo restores the original tree.
The Page root cannot be wrapped and the status bar says so.

title: Right-click context menu on the canvas and in Layers
steps: Insert a Container and a Paragraph after it.
Right-click the Paragraph on the canvas.
Move through the items with ArrowDown and ArrowUp and run one with Enter.
Hover each item to read its tooltip, then run each enabled item on a Paragraph inside a Section.
Right-click a row in Layers and press Escape.
Right-click an element near the right edge of the canvas.
expected: Right-click selects the element and opens a menu at the pointer that contains at least, in this order, Rename [command.rename], Copy [command.copy], Cut [command.cut], Paste [command.paste], Duplicate [command.duplicate], Move up [command.moveUp], Move down [command.moveDown], Wrap in a row [command.wrapRow], Wrap in a column [command.wrapColumn], Remove wrapper [command.unwrap], Make child of previous layer [command.nestIntoPrevious], Move out of parent [command.promote], Take into the hand [command.takeIntoHand], Lock [command.lock], Hide [command.hide] and Delete [command.delete]; later entries may add items.

Each item has a tooltip naming its action and its shortcut where it has one, and runs the same command as its shortcut or menu row, producing the same document JSON; items that cannot apply to the selection are disabled; items whose feature is not built yet are disabled and labelled 'not available yet' [common.notAvailableYet] — which features are built is read from one feature registry, and the test checks the UI against that registry instead of a fixed list, so it stays valid as later entries are built.
The menu is operable with ArrowUp/ArrowDown and Enter, closes with Escape or a click outside, and always stays fully inside the window.
The same menu opens on Layers rows.

title: Nest the selection into its previous sibling
steps: Insert a Container, then a Paragraph after it, both in Page.
Right-click the Paragraph and choose 'Make child of previous layer' [command.nestIntoPrevious].
Right-click the Container, which has no previous sibling, and open the same menu.
expected: The Paragraph becomes the last child of the Container in the document JSON and stays selected.
When there is no previous sibling, or the previous sibling cannot contain the element, the command is disabled and the document JSON is unchanged.
One undo restores the original tree.

title: Move the selection out of its parent with P
steps: Insert a Section containing a Container that contains a Paragraph.
Select the Paragraph on the canvas and press P.
Right-click the Paragraph and choose 'Move out of parent' [command.promote].
Select a direct child of Page and press P.
expected: P and the 'Move out of parent' [command.promote] menu item move the element into its grandparent, directly after its former parent, in the document JSON.
The status bar reads 'Promoted <name> into <parent>, position N' [status.promoted].
A direct child of Page cannot be promoted and the status bar says there is nothing to promote to.
Each promotion is one undo step and the element stays selected.

title: Duplicate the selection with Ctrl+D
steps: Insert a Section with a Heading and a Paragraph.
Select the Section and press Ctrl+D.
expected: A deep copy of the Section with its children, texts and styles is inserted directly after it in the document JSON.
Every node of the copy has a new unique id and a unique name.
The copy is selected and the duplicate is one undo step.

title: Copy and paste elements through the system clipboard with Ctrl+C and Ctrl+V
steps: Insert a Section with a Heading, and an empty Container after the Section.
Select the Heading, press Ctrl+C.
Select the Container and press Ctrl+V.
Select the Section and press Ctrl+V.
Read the system clipboard.
expected: Ctrl+C writes the selected element to the system clipboard in the app's element format (its subtree with texts and styles); nothing is kept only in memory, and reading the system clipboard after Ctrl+C returns that element.
Ctrl+V reads the system clipboard: with a container selected the copy is appended as its last child; with a non-container selected it is inserted right after it.
The pasted subtree has new ids and unique names, and the same styles and text as the source.
The pasted element is selected and each paste is one undo step.

title: Walk the tree with the arrow keys
steps: Insert a Section with a Heading and a Paragraph.
Select the Heading on the canvas.
Press ArrowRight, ArrowLeft, ArrowUp, ArrowDown, and ArrowUp twice.
expected: ArrowRight selects the next sibling and ArrowLeft the previous one; ArrowUp selects the parent; ArrowDown selects the first child.
The status bar announces each move, e.g. 'Paragraph selected. Sibling 2 of 2.' [status.walk.sibling].
At the ends and at the Page root the selection stays and the status bar explains why.
Walking never changes the document JSON.

title: Take the selection into the hand with M and place it with the keyboard
steps: Insert a Section with a Heading and a Paragraph, and a Container after the Section.
Select the Heading and press M.
Press ArrowDown, then ArrowUp to climb a level, then ArrowLeft to descend, then Enter.
Select the Paragraph, press M, move the aim and press Escape.
expected: After M the status bar reads 'Holding <name>. Arrows aim, Enter places, Esc drops.' [status.hand.holding] and the canvas shows the same insertion indicator a mouse drag shows.
ArrowDown/ArrowRight aim at the next position, ArrowUp climbs a receiver level, ArrowLeft descends; the status bar names the receiver, position and level after each key.
Enter moves the element to the aimed place in the document JSON (one undo step).
Escape drops the hand and leaves the document JSON unchanged.

title: Edit text in place with double-click or Enter
steps: Insert a Paragraph.
Double-click it on the canvas, select all, type 'Hello world' and press Enter.
Press Enter on the selected Paragraph, type more text and press Escape.
Double-click it, type text and click elsewhere on the canvas.
expected: Double-click or Enter makes the element's text editable in place with a caret; the status bar says 'Editing text — Enter or click away to keep it, Escape to cancel' [status.textEdit.editing].
Enter or clicking away writes the new text into the document JSON as one undo step.
Escape restores the text that was there before editing and leaves the document JSON unchanged.
While editing, Delete, arrow keys and letter shortcuts act on the text, not on the tree.

title: Bold, italic and links inside text with Ctrl+B, Ctrl+I and Ctrl+K
steps: Insert a Paragraph and double-click it.
Select a word and press Ctrl+B; select another word and press Ctrl+I.
Select a word, press Ctrl+K and enter https://example.com.
Select the bold word and press Ctrl+B again.
Put HTML with bold, italic, a link, a heading and a script on the system clipboard, paste it and press Enter.
expected: Ctrl+B wraps the selection in <strong>, Ctrl+I in <em>, Ctrl+K in <a href>; pressing the shortcut again inside the mark removes it.
Pasted content keeps the supported marks (strong, em, and links with safe URLs) and drops everything else: other tags become their plain text and scripts are removed.
After Enter the document JSON stores the text as a tree of plain strings, strong, em and a nodes; unsafe URLs such as javascript: are refused.

title: Rename an element with F2 or inline in Layers
steps: Insert a Section.
Select it on the canvas, press F2, type 'Intro' and press Enter.
Double-click its row in Layers, type 'Hero' and press Enter.
Double-click the row again, clear the name and press Enter; do it again and press Escape.
expected: F2 edits the selection's name in place in its Layers row, the same inline edit as double-clicking the row name, with the current name selected; no dialog opens.
Enter commits the new name into the document JSON; Escape cancels.
An empty name keeps the previous name.
The new name appears in Layers and on the canvas label; each rename is one undo step.

title: Select several elements with Shift+click and Ctrl+click
steps: Insert a Section with a Heading and two Paragraphs.
Click the Heading, Shift+click the first Paragraph, Shift+click the second Paragraph.
Ctrl+click the first Paragraph.
Shift+click a row in Layers.
Press Escape.
expected: Shift+click adds to the selection and Ctrl+click toggles an element in or out; each selected element has its own outline and its Layers row is highlighted.
The canvas label reads 'N elements' [canvas.label.selectionCount].
Shift+click in Layers adds to the selection the same way.
Escape clears the whole selection.

title: Remove a wrapper and lift its children into its place
steps: Insert a Section containing a Container with a Heading and a Paragraph.
Right-click the Container and choose 'Remove wrapper' [command.unwrap].
Undo, right-click the Page root and open the same menu.
expected: The Container disappears from the document JSON and the Heading and Paragraph take its index in the Section, in their original order.
The lifted children become the selection.
The command is unavailable for the Page root and for elements without children.
One undo restores the Container with its children.

title: Select elements by dragging a marquee on the page
steps: Insert a Section with a Heading and two Paragraphs.
Press on empty page area below the Section and drag a rectangle over the Heading and first Paragraph, then release.
Hold Shift and drag another rectangle over the second Paragraph.
Hold Ctrl and drag a rectangle over the Heading.
expected: While dragging a translucent rectangle follows the pointer.
On release every element the rectangle touches, except the elements that contain the start point, is selected; the status bar reads 'N elements selected.' [status.selection.count].
Shift adds to the existing selection; Ctrl toggles the touched elements.
Pressing on an element starts a move drag, never a marquee.

title: Delete, move and duplicate several selected elements at once
steps: Insert a Section with a Heading and three Paragraphs.
Select two Paragraphs and press Alt+ArrowUp.
Press Ctrl+D.
Press Delete.
Select the Heading and the last Paragraph and press R; undo; press C.
Select a Paragraph and the Section and press R.
Select two Paragraphs and press P.
expected: Alt+ArrowUp moves every selected element one position up keeping their relative order.
Ctrl+D duplicates each selected element right after itself; Delete removes all of them; each is one undo step.

R (or C) with several siblings of one parent selected wraps them together in one new Row (or Column) placed where the first of them was, keeping their order, as one undo step; a selection whose elements have different parents is refused with 'These elements must share a parent' [status.wrap.needsSameParent] and the document JSON is unchanged.
Commands that need a single element (promote, hand, rename, edit text) are refused with 'This needs a single selection' [status.needsSingleSelection] and the document JSON is unchanged.

title: Select every element in the current container with Ctrl+A
steps: Insert a Section with three Paragraphs, and a Container after the Section.
Select the second Paragraph on the canvas and press Ctrl+A.
Press Escape, then press Ctrl+A with nothing selected.
Double-click a Paragraph to edit its text and press Ctrl+A.
expected: With an element selected, Ctrl+A selects it and all its siblings (the three Paragraphs).
With nothing selected, Ctrl+A selects every child of Page.
While editing text Ctrl+A selects the text and does not change the element selection.
The document JSON never changes.

title: Lock an element so it cannot be moved, edited or deleted
steps: Insert a Section with a Paragraph.
Lock the Section with the lock toggle on its Layers row.
Try to drag the Section, drag its Paragraph, press Delete, press R, double-click the Paragraph text.
Unlock it.
expected: The lock flag is stored in the document JSON and a lock icon shows on the row.
Every structural change to the locked element or its descendants is refused with a status message such as 'Unlock <name> before deleting it' [status.locked.delete]; the document JSON does not change.
Locked elements can still be selected.
Unlocking restores all actions; lock and unlock are undo steps.

title: Hide and show an element
steps: Insert a Section with two Paragraphs.
Click the eye toggle on the first Paragraph's Layers row.
Click it again.
expected: The hidden flag is stored in the document JSON; the element has computed display:none in the iframe and its row is dimmed with a crossed eye.
Hidden elements can still be selected from Layers.
Showing it restores its layout exactly; both actions are undo steps.

title: Application menu: File, Edit, Arrange, View, Help, Theme and Language
steps: Open the app menu from the logo button.
Open each submenu with the mouse, then again with Enter and the arrow keys.
Run Undo from Edit, and 'Wrap in a row' [command.wrapRow] from Arrange with a Paragraph selected.
Open File and look at an item whose feature is not built yet.
expected: File [menu.file] has Save project [command.saveProject], Open project [command.openProject], Open folder [command.openFolder], Import HTML [command.importHtml], Export page [command.exportPage], New blank page [command.newBlankPage] and Commands [command.commandBar]; Edit [menu.edit] has Undo [command.undo], Redo [command.redo], Duplicate [command.duplicate], Copy [command.copy], Cut [command.cut], Paste [command.paste], Delete [command.delete], Select all in container [command.selectAllInContainer] and Clear the selection [command.clearSelection]; Arrange [menu.arrange] has Move up [command.moveUp], Move down [command.moveDown], Wrap in a row [command.wrapRow], Wrap in a column [command.wrapColumn], Remove wrapper [command.unwrap], Make child of previous layer [command.nestIntoPrevious], Move out of parent [command.promote], Take into the hand [command.takeIntoHand] and Rename [command.rename].

View [menu.view] has toggles for the Elements [panel.elements], Layers [panel.layers], Inspector [panel.inspector], Explorer [panel.explorer], Code [panel.code], Timeline [panel.timeline], Variables [panel.variables], Checks [panel.checks] and Workbench [panel.workbench] panels, Guides & Grids [panel.guidesGrids], Canvas tools [panel.canvasTools], Toggle left dock (Ctrl+B) [command.toggleLeftDock], Toggle inspector (Ctrl+Alt+B) [command.toggleInspector], Collapse every dock (Ctrl+\) [command.collapseDocks], Developer tools [command.developerTools] and Reset workspace [command.resetWorkspace]; Help [menu.help] has Keyboard shortcuts [panel.shortcuts]; Theme [menu.theme] has Light [theme.light], Dark [theme.dark] and System [theme.system]; Language [menu.language] has Português (Brasil) [language.ptBR] and English [language.en].

Each item shows its shortcut where it has one and runs the same command as the shortcut, producing the same document JSON; items that cannot apply now are disabled; items whose feature is not built yet are disabled and labelled 'not available yet' [common.notAvailableYet] — which features are built is read from one feature registry, and the test checks the UI against that registry instead of a fixed list, so it stays valid as later entries are built.
The menu opens with Enter or ArrowDown, moves with the arrow keys, closes with Escape and returns focus to the logo button.

title: UI language: Brazilian Portuguese by default, English available
steps: Open the app with a fresh profile.
Switch the UI language to English from the app menu, then back to Português (Brasil).
Reload.
expected: A fresh profile shows every UI text in pt-BR: menus, panels, tooltips, status bar messages and accessible names.
Switching the language re-renders every visible text without a reload; the choice is stored in the preferences store and restored after reload.
A unit test proves that the pt-BR and en catalogues have the same keys with the same placeholders.
Tests that assert UI text set the language explicitly or read the text through its i18n key.

title: Autosave to IndexedDB and restore the work after a reload
steps: Insert a Section with a Heading, edit the Heading text and select the Heading.
Wait for the status bar to read 'Saved' [status.save.saved].
Reload the page.
expected: After each change the status bar shows 'Saving…' [status.save.saving] and then 'Saved' [status.save.saved] when the project record in IndexedDB matches the document JSON.
After the reload the document JSON and the selection are exactly what they were.
A fresh profile with no saved record shows an empty page and 'Not saved' [status.save.notSaved].

title: Never lose an edit that is not yet saved
steps: Insert a Section and reload the page immediately, before the autosave delay has passed.
Make another change and try to close the tab while the status bar still reads 'Saving…' [status.save.saving].
Make a change, switch to another tab and back, then reload.
expected: Pending changes are written to IndexedDB on pagehide and visibilitychange, so the Section is present after the immediate reload.
Closing or reloading while a save is pending or has failed triggers the browser's leave-page confirmation; once the status reads 'Saved' [status.save.saved] no confirmation appears.
If IndexedDB refuses a write, the status bar reads 'Not saved' [status.save.notSaved] with the reason and the change stays in memory until a later write succeeds.

title: Keep saved versions and restore the work after a crash
steps: Build a page with a few elements and wait for Saved; make 12 more changes, waiting for Saved after each.
Close the browser process without a clean unload and open the app again.
expected: The app keeps the last 10 saved versions of the project in IndexedDB, each with its time.
After the crash the last saved document is restored and a notice says the work was recovered.

title: Start over with a new blank page
steps: Build a page with a few elements.
Choose File > New blank page and cancel the confirmation.
Choose File > New blank page and confirm.
expected: Cancel leaves the document JSON unchanged.
Confirming replaces the page with an empty Page root.
Selection and undo history are cleared and the empty-page hint shows.
The status bar reads that a blank page was created and the blank page is autosaved.

title: Recover from a corrupted saved project
steps: Build a page and wait for Saved.
Corrupt the current project record in IndexedDB and reload.
Open the recovery dialog and restore the newest earlier version.
expected: A corrupted current record is left untouched in storage; the app opens with the status 'Recovery required' [status.save.recoveryRequired] and a dialog listing earlier versions with their times.
Restoring a version loads exactly that document JSON and it becomes the current saved record.
Until something is restored or a new page is started, autosave does not overwrite the corrupted record.

title: Only one tab edits the project at a time
steps: Open the app, build a page and wait for Saved.
Open the app in a second tab.
In the second tab click 'Take over editing' [tabGuard.takeOver].
Go back to the first tab and try to insert an element.
expected: A tab that opens while another tab is editing shows the project read-only with a notice and a 'Take over editing' [tabGuard.takeOver] button; it never writes to IndexedDB.
Taking over reloads the latest saved project in that tab and makes the other tab read-only with a notice (tabs coordinate with BroadcastChannel).
A read-only tab refuses every document command with a status message, so autosave from two tabs never interleaves.

title: Save the project as one archive file
steps: Build a page with a few elements and styles.
Choose File > Save project.
expected: A single project archive 'project.zip' is downloaded; it holds project.json and every file the project stores next to the document, at its path, so files added by later features are saved with the project.
project.json contains the format version and the whole document JSON (its page trees and every setting it holds), and nothing that depends on the editor session (no selection, no zoom, no DOM ids).
Saving the same document twice produces byte-identical archives apart from the saved timestamp.

title: Open a project archive
steps: Save a project to a file, then change the page.
Choose File > Open project, pick the saved archive and cancel the confirmation; do it again and confirm.
Choose File > Open project and pick a file that is not a valid project archive, then an archive whose format version is newer than the app's.
expected: Before replacing the current project a confirmation asks; Cancel leaves the document JSON unchanged.
Opening the saved archive restores exactly the saved document JSON and every file the archive holds.
An invalid file shows an error dialog naming the problem and leaves the current document JSON unchanged.
An archive with a newer or unknown format version is refused with an error naming the version, and the current document JSON is unchanged.
After opening, the undo history is empty and the project is autosaved.

title: Inspector shows the selection's identity and collapsible property sections
steps: With nothing selected, look at the Inspector.
Insert a Section with a Paragraph and select the Paragraph.
Collapse the Text section, select the Section, then select the Paragraph again.
expected: With nothing selected the Inspector shows 'Nothing selected' [inspector.nothingSelected], short hints and a Page properties button (disabled and labelled 'not available yet' [common.notAvailableYet] until page properties are built — which features are built is read from one feature registry, and the test checks the UI against that registry instead of a fixed list, so it stays valid as later entries are built).

With an element selected it shows the element icon, name and tag, and, in this order, the sections that apply to the element type among Content, Layout, Space, Size, Position, Paint, Border, Text and Effects; later entries may add sections after Effects. Each section header summarises its current values (e.g. Layout: block, Size: auto x auto).
Sections collapse and expand; the collapsed state is remembered per section across selections and reloads.
For text elements the Content section shows the text in a field; editing it there updates the canvas and the document JSON as one undo step.
The element actions menu in the inspector header offers Lock and Hide, which run the same commands as the Layers toggles.

title: Numeric property fields, built with the Size section's Width and Height: typing, units, steppers and scrubbing
steps: Select a Container.
Type 24 in Width and press Enter; change its unit to %; type 'auto'.
Press ArrowUp, Shift+ArrowUp and Alt+ArrowUp in the field; click the step buttons.
Drag the field label to the right by 50 px; repeat with Shift and with Alt.
Type 'abc' and press Enter; type 30 and press Escape.
expected: Enter writes the value with its unit into the document JSON and the computed style in the iframe matches it.
The unit menu offers px, %, em, rem, vw, vh and the keywords valid for the property (auto, fit-content, min-content, max-content where valid).
ArrowUp/ArrowDown step by 1, with Shift by 10, with Alt by 0.1; dragging the label scrubs with the same multipliers.
Invalid input is rejected with a message and the previous value stays; Escape restores the previous value.
A whole scrub gesture or one typed commit is exactly one undo step.
Delete, Backspace, arrows, letters and Ctrl+Z typed in a field act on the field, never on the canvas selection or the document history.

title: Edit display with every keyword
steps: Select a Container.
Set display to each of block, inline, inline-block, flex, inline-flex, grid, inline-grid, contents and none.
expected: The Display control offers every keyword the property catalogue has for display, and nothing else (a unit test checks that the control options equal the catalogue keyword list).
Each choice writes the value into the document JSON and the element's computed display matches.

title: Flex container controls: direction, wrap, alignment matrix and gap
steps: Insert a Container, set its display to flex and insert three Paragraphs into it.
Click each direction arrow (row, row-reverse, column, column-reverse).
Set wrap; click each cell of the 3x3 alignment matrix; click Stretch and Spread.
Set gap, row-gap and column-gap.
expected: The flex controls appear in the Layout section when display is flex or inline-flex.
The direction arrows set flex-direction; wrap sets flex-wrap (nowrap, wrap, wrap-reverse).
Each matrix cell sets justify-content and align-items together, mapped to the current direction; Stretch sets align-items:stretch and Spread sets justify-content:space-between.
align-content offers every catalogue keyword.
Gap values are written to the document JSON and the measured distance between the children in the iframe equals the gap.

title: Grid container controls: column and row tracks, gap and auto flow
steps: Select a Container, set display:grid and insert four Paragraphs into it.
Click 'Add a column' [inspector.grid.addColumn] three times, change the second track to 2fr and the third to 200px.
Edit the track expression text to 'repeat(4, minmax(0, 1fr))'.
Set rows, gap, grid-auto-flow, justify-items and grid-template-areas.
expected: The grid controls appear in the Layout section when display is grid or inline-grid.
The track editor shows one chip per column track and writes grid-template-columns (e.g. '1fr 2fr 200px').
Typing a track expression replaces the tracks and the chips update to match.
Measured column widths of the children in the iframe match the tracks.
Rows, gap, auto flow, justify-items and template areas are written to the document JSON.

title: Child-of-flex and child-of-grid controls (In parent)
steps: Inside a flex Container select a child; set flex-grow, flex-shrink, flex-basis, align-self and order.
Inside a grid Container select a child; set grid-column '1 / 3', grid-row and justify-self.
expected: An 'In parent' [inspector.group.inParent] group appears only when the parent is flex or grid and shows the item properties that apply to that parent type.
Each value is written to the document JSON and changes the measured geometry of the child as CSS predicts.

title: Margin and padding with the box model editor
steps: Select a Section.
Click the top padding number in the box model diagram and type 32.
Turn on 'Link all four sides' [inspector.spacing.linkAll] for margin and type 16.
Set a negative margin-left; try a negative padding.
Change the padding unit to rem.
expected: The box model diagram shows margin, padding and the element size; each side is editable in place.
Linked sides change together and write the margin shorthand; unlinked sides write per-side values.
Negative margins are accepted; negative padding is rejected with a message.
Computed margin and padding in the iframe match the document JSON.

title: Size, min/max, box sizing, aspect ratio and overflow
steps: Select a Container.
Set width 50%, height 200px, min-width 100px, max-width 600px, min-height and max-height.
Set box-sizing to content-box, aspect-ratio 16 / 9, overflow hidden, overflow-x and overflow-y.
expected: Each value is written to the document JSON and the computed style matches.
The measured size of the element in the iframe matches the values (e.g. width is 50% of the parent's content box).
The Size section summary reads the current width x height.

title: Position mode, offsets, z-index, float and clear
steps: Select a Paragraph inside a Section.
Click each position button: static, relative, absolute, fixed, sticky.
With relative, set top 10px and left 20px; set z-index 5.
Set float and clear.
expected: The position buttons write position; offset fields top/right/bottom/left appear when position is not static.
The measured position of the element in the iframe moves by the offsets.
z-index, float and clear are written to the document JSON and the computed style matches.
The test checks only the properties this entry sets (position, offsets, z-index, float, clear), not the whole style bag.

title: Colour picker: area, sliders, HSB/RGB/Hex fields, preview, Apply and Cancel
steps: Select a Container and open the background colour picker in the Paint section.
Drag in the saturation/brightness area, drag the hue and alpha sliders.
Switch the format between HSB, RGB and Hex and type values in each.
Click Apply; open it again, change the colour and click Cancel.
Select a Paragraph and open the text colour picker in the Text section.
expected: This entry adds the background-color field (Paint) and the color field (Text); both open the picker.
The picker shows the previous and current colour, the saturation/brightness area, hue and alpha sliders, a text field and per-channel fields for the chosen format.
The canvas previews the colour live while dragging; Apply writes it to the document JSON as one undo step; Cancel restores the previous value.
Invalid channel values are rejected.
Both fields open the same picker component; the codebase has exactly one colour picker, which every later colour field reuses (evaluator checks the diff).

title: Colour picker: OKLCH and OKLab formats and CSS colour text
steps: Open a colour picker.
Switch the format to OKLCH and OKLab and type values in each.
Type 'rebeccapurple', '#0f172a80', 'rgb(10 20 30 / 50%)' and 'oklch(70% 0.15 260)' in the text field.
Type 'notacolour'.
expected: OKLCH and OKLab channel fields convert to and from the same colour shown in the other formats.

Named colours, hex with 3, 4, 6 and 8 digits, rgb(), hsl(), hwb(), lab(), lch(), oklab(), oklch() and color() are parsed; the stored value is the text the user chose; colours outside sRGB show a gamut warning.
Invalid text is rejected with a message and the previous colour stays.

title: Saved and recent colours and the eyedropper
steps: Open a colour picker, pick a colour and click 'Save current' [colorPicker.saveCurrent].
Apply a few different colours to different elements.
Open the picker and click a saved swatch and a recent swatch.
Click the eyedropper button and pick a colour.
expected: Saved colours are stored with the project and listed in every picker; recent colours list the last 10 applied colours.
Clicking a swatch sets the current colour.
The eyedropper uses Chrome's EyeDropper API and sets the current colour to the sRGBHex it returns (the test stubs window.EyeDropper); without the API the button is hidden.

title: Text properties: font, size, weight, style, spacing, alignment, colour and decoration
steps: Select a Paragraph.
Set font family, size 18px, weight 600, italic, line-height 1.6, letter-spacing 0.02em and word-spacing.
Click each text-align button (left, right, centre, justify, start, end).
Set color, text-decoration, text-transform, text-indent, text-overflow, white-space, word-break and vertical-align.
expected: The font menu lists system and web-safe font stacks; weight offers 100-900 with names.
Every value is written to the document JSON and the computed style of the paragraph in the iframe matches.
Each keyword control offers every keyword the property catalogue defines for it.
Each value is written by one command per property, and every other control for the same property must use that command.

title: Advanced text properties
steps: Select a Paragraph.
Set font-stretch, font-variant, font-feature-settings, overflow-wrap, hyphens, line clamp 2, direction rtl, writing-mode and text-orientation.
expected: Each value is written to the document JSON and the computed style matches.
Line clamp 2 limits the measured paragraph height to two lines of text.

title: Background colour, image, size, position, repeat and more
steps: Select a Section.
Set a background colour, a background image URL, size cover, position center, repeat no-repeat and attachment fixed.
Set background-origin, background-clip and background-blend-mode.
expected: Each value is written to the document JSON and the computed background of the section in the iframe matches.
The Paint section summary shows the colour swatch or 'None' [inspector.summary.none].

title: Gradient editor: linear, radial and conic gradients with stops
steps: Select a Section and click 'Add a gradient' [inspector.gradient.add].
Switch between Linear, Radial and Conic.
Drag a stop, click the bar to add a stop, change a stop colour and position, delete a stop.
Change the angle, click reverse and distribute evenly.
expected: The gradient bar previews the gradient with draggable stop handles.
The CSS text of the gradient is shown and written to background-image in the document JSON after each change.
The computed background-image in the iframe equals that text.
Removing the gradient returns background-image to none.
Every gradient change is written by one command, and every other control for the background fill must use that command.

title: Borders per side, radius per corner and outline
steps: Select a Container.
Set border width 2px, style solid, colour red for all sides.
Select only the Top edge and set it to 4px dashed.
Set radius 12px for all corners, then unlink and set the top-left corner to 24px.
Set outline and outline-offset.
expected: The border style control offers every catalogue keyword (none, solid, dashed, dotted, double, groove, ridge, inset, outset, hidden).
All-sides edits write the shorthand; single-edge edits write that side only; the computed borders in the iframe match.
Per-corner radius values are written and the computed border radii match.
Outline and outline-offset are written and computed as set.
Each value is written by one command per property, and every other control for the same property must use that command.

title: Opacity, visibility, cursor, pointer events, selection and blend mode
steps: Select a Container.
Drag the opacity slider to 50%.
Set visibility hidden, cursor pointer, pointer-events none, user-select none, mix-blend-mode multiply and isolation isolate.
expected: Opacity 50% is written as 0.5 and the computed opacity matches.
Each other value is written to the document JSON and the computed style matches.
Each value is written by one command per property, and every other control for the same property must use that command.

title: Box shadow and text shadow editor
steps: Select a Container and click 'Add a shadow' [inspector.shadow.add].
Drag the light pad; set X, Y, blur, spread, colour and inset.
Add a second shadow, hide the first, remove the second.
Select a Paragraph and set a text shadow.
expected: Each shadow layer has X, Y, blur, spread, colour and inset controls; dragging the light pad sets X and Y.
The box-shadow list is written to the document JSON in layer order; hidden layers are left out of the CSS.
The computed box-shadow and text-shadow in the iframe match.

title: Filters, backdrop filter, clip path and mask
steps: Select a Container with a background colour and a Paragraph inside.
Set blur, brightness, contrast, saturate, hue-rotate, grayscale, invert and sepia with their sliders.
Set backdrop-filter, clip-path and mask-image.
expected: The filter sliders compose one filter value in a fixed order and write it to the document JSON; the computed filter matches.
A 'Remove filters' [inspector.filters.remove] button in the filter group removes the filter property from the document JSON.
backdrop-filter, clip-path and mask-image are written and computed as set.
Each value is written by one command per property, and every other control for the same property must use that command.

title: Move, rotate, scale, skew, origin and 3D transform properties
steps: Select a Container.
Set Move X 20px, Move Y 10px, Rotate 15deg, Scale 1.2, Skew X 5deg, Skew Y 0.
Set transform-origin, perspective, perspective-origin, transform-style, backface-visibility and transform-box.
expected: The transform fields compose one transform value written to the document JSON; the computed transform matrix in the iframe matches it.
The other transform properties are written and computed as set.
Move X/Y, Rotate, Scale and Skew are written by one transform command that composes the transform value, and every other control of the transform (on the canvas or elsewhere) must use that command.

title: Transition and will-change
steps: Select a Container.
Set transition 'background-color 200ms ease-in-out' and will-change 'transform'.
expected: The transition text is validated as CSS and written to the document JSON; the computed transition matches.
will-change offers the catalogue keywords and accepts a property name.

title: Remaining advanced properties
steps: Select a Container.
Set contain, content-visibility, columns, column-span, column-fill, column-rule width/style/colour, break-before, break-after, break-inside.
Set scroll-behavior, overscroll-behavior, scroll-snap-type, scroll-snap-align, counter-reset, counter-increment and all.
expected: Every property listed is present in the inspector with the control type the catalogue declares (keyword menu, length or text).
Each value is written to the document JSON and the computed style matches.
touch-action (touch devices only) and content (it acts only on ::before and ::after, which the editor cannot target) are not offered.

title: ID, classes, title and custom declarations of an element
steps: Select a Section.
Type 'intro' in ID; type an ID already used by another element; type '1abc'.
Add the classes 'dark wide' in Classes.
Type 'title' text and custom CSS declarations 'scroll-margin-top: 80px'.
expected: These fields sit in the Content section under an Attributes heading.
The ID is written to the document JSON; duplicate or invalid IDs are rejected with a message.
Classes are stored as a list; custom declarations are validated and stored with the element's styles.
Nothing typed here ever produces a style attribute on the element in the iframe markup.

title: Mark set values and reset one property or all of them
steps: Select a Paragraph and set its padding, color and font size.
Reset the color with its reset control.
Run 'Reset every value' [command.resetAllValues] from the element actions menu.
expected: Every property with a value set on this element shows a dot; each section header shows the number of values set as a separate badge next to its summary, and the summary text itself is unchanged.
Resetting a property removes it from the element styles in the document JSON and the field shows the inherited or default value in a muted style.
The element actions menu gains 'Reset every value' [command.resetAllValues], which removes all style values of the element in one undo step.

title: Search the inspector for a property
steps: Select a Container.
Type 'radius' in Search properties.
Type 'padding-left'.
Clear the search.
expected: Only properties whose label or CSS name matches are shown, inside their sections, with the matched text highlighted.
A search with no match says so.
Clearing the search restores the previous sections and their collapsed state.

title: Switch the inspector between all properties and essentials only
steps: Select a Paragraph.
Click 'Essentials only' [inspector.mode.essentials] at the bottom of the inspector.
Set a value on a non-essential property, click 'All properties' [inspector.mode.all], then 'Essentials only' [inspector.mode.essentials] again.
Reload.
expected: By default the inspector shows every property of the catalogue that applies to the element, grouped by section; this stays the default.

Essentials only shows the common subset (display, flex/grid basics, margin, padding, width, height, position, colour, background, border, radius, font family, size, weight, line height, alignment, opacity, shadow).
A property with a value set is always shown in essentials too.
The chosen mode is remembered across reloads; a fresh profile starts with all properties.

title: Add a property that is not shown yet
steps: Select a Container in essentials mode.
Click the + button in the inspector header.
Type 'aspect' and choose aspect-ratio.
expected: The + menu lists the applicable properties not currently shown, grouped by section, with label and CSS name, filterable by typing.
Choosing one reveals that field in its section and focuses it.

title: Switch an element between equivalent semantic tags
steps: Insert a Section with children and styles.
Change its tag to article, then header, then div.
Select a Heading and change its level from h2 to h1 and h4.
Select a Paragraph and switch it to span and pre.
expected: The tag menu lists only the tags equivalent to the element (div, section, header, main, footer, nav, aside, article for containers; h1-h6 for headings; p, span, pre for text).
Switching keeps children, text, name and styles; the iframe renders the new tag.
Each switch is one undo step.

title: Floating quick panel over the selection
steps: Select a Section.
Read the quick panel above it; type a new W and H value; change the tag menu; click Fill and pick a colour, then switch the fill to a gradient.
Select a Paragraph and change Size and Text colour in the quick panel.
Set Border, Opacity, Effects (blur) and Transform (Move X, Rotate, Scale) from the quick panel.
Click More actions.
Drag the quick panel by its handle to another spot, select another element and come back.
Select the first element at the very top of the page.
expected: The quick panel shows the tag menu, a drag handle, a More actions button, W and H, Fill, Text colour and font Size for text elements, Border, Opacity, Effects, Transform and the 'Edit on canvas' [quickPanel.editOnCanvas] mode menu; controls and modes whose feature is not built yet are disabled and labelled 'not available yet' [common.notAvailableYet] — which features are built is read from one feature registry, and the test checks the UI against that registry instead of a fixed list, so it stays valid as later entries are built.

Every quick panel control runs the same command as the matching inspector field and writes the same document JSON, and both stay in sync; Fill opens the same fill editor as the inspector (solid colour or gradient), and Transform writes the same transform value as the inspector's transform fields.
More actions opens the element's context menu at the button: the same menu as a right-click on the element.
A dragged quick panel keeps its offset for that element.
The quick panel is always placed inside the canvas viewport; with no room above the element it goes below it.

title: Edit a property on several selected elements at once
steps: Insert three Paragraphs with different font sizes and select all three.
Look at Size in the quick panel and the inspector.
Type 20 in Size and press Enter.
Press Ctrl+Z.
expected: Fields whose values differ between the selected elements show 'Mixed' [inspector.mixed]; equal values are shown normally.
A committed value is written to every selected element in the document JSON as one undo step.
Undo restores each element's own previous value.

title: Resize an element with its eight handles
steps: Select a Container with a fixed size.
Drag the E handle 100 screen px left, the S handle 80 px down, the SE handle diagonally.
Drag the SE handle with Shift held.
Drag the W handle with Alt held.
expected: Eight handles sit on the corners and edge centres of the selection outline.
Edge handles change one dimension and corner handles both; the change in CSS px equals the pointer movement divided by the zoom; width and height are written to the document JSON.
Shift keeps the aspect ratio; Alt resizes symmetrically around the centre.
The status bar shows the live size while dragging and 'Resized to W x H' [status.resized] at the end; each resize is one undo step.

title: Edit padding and margin by dragging on the canvas
steps: Select a Section and choose Padding in 'Edit on canvas' [quickPanel.editOnCanvas].
Drag the top padding band down by 20 screen px.
Drag the left band with Alt held; drag the bottom band with Shift held.
Choose Margin and drag the top margin band.
expected: In Padding or Margin mode the four sides are drawn as bands with their values.
Dragging a band changes only that side; Alt changes the opposite side by the same amount; Shift changes all four sides.
The status bar shows the live value; the value is written to the document JSON as one undo step.

title: Edit radius, border width and gaps by dragging on the canvas
steps: Select a Container and choose Radius in 'Edit on canvas' [quickPanel.editOnCanvas]; drag the corner handle inward.
Choose Border and drag an edge handle.
Select a flex Container with children; choose Gap, Row gap and Column gap and drag the gap bands.
expected: Radius mode shows a corner handle labelled with the current radius and writes border-radius.
Border mode writes border width of the dragged side.
Gap modes show bands between children and write gap, row-gap or column-gap; the measured distance between children in the iframe matches.

title: Edit shadow offset and blur by dragging on the canvas
steps: Select a Container with a box shadow.
Choose Shadow offset in 'Edit on canvas' [quickPanel.editOnCanvas] and drag the handle.
Choose Shadow blur and drag the handle.
Select a Paragraph with a text shadow and repeat both modes.
expected: Shadow offset mode moves the first shadow's X and Y with the pointer; Shadow blur mode changes its blur.
On a text element with a text shadow the same modes edit the first text shadow: X, Y and blur.
The box-shadow or text-shadow in the document JSON and the computed style update; each drag is one undo step.

title: Page properties: title, language, direction and page styles
steps: Click Page in the top bar (or Page properties in the empty inspector).
Set the title 'Landing', language 'pt-BR', direction rtl.
Set the page background colour, text colour and base font.
expected: The Page root is selected and the inspector shows page settings above the page styles.
Title, language and direction are stored in the page settings of the document JSON; the iframe html element gets lang and dir.
Page background, colour and font are stored on the Page root styles and computed in the iframe.

title: Export the page as a ZIP with HTML and a separate CSS file
steps: Build a page with a Section, a Heading with bold text, a Paragraph containing a link made with Ctrl+K, a Container with padding and a hidden Paragraph, with page title and language set.
Click Export.
expected: A ZIP is downloaded containing index.html and css/styles.css, and index.html links css/styles.css.
index.html has a doctype, <html lang dir>, <meta charset>, viewport meta and the page <title>; every node is written with its semantic tag, text is escaped and inline marks are kept.
No element in index.html has a style attribute, an editor-generated data-* attribute or an editor-generated id; hidden elements carry the hidden attribute.

The exported page opened in Chrome renders every element with the same computed styles as the canvas, apart from editor-only aids (empty-container minimum height, closed details and dialogs shown while selected, selection chrome).

title: Design tokens as CSS variables
steps: Open the Variables panel and create a colour, a spacing and a font-size variable.
Use the colour variable as a Section's background and the spacing variable as its padding.
Change the colour variable.
expected: Variables are stored in the project; colour, length and font fields offer them next to typed values.
Every element that uses a variable updates when it changes, as one undo step.
The export writes the variables in :root and uses var(--name) where they are used.

title: Exported CSS uses readable BEM classes and is deterministic
steps: Build a page with a Section named 'Hero' containing a styled Heading 'Title' and a styled Paragraph 'Call to action', plus a second element with the same name.
Add user classes to one element.
Export twice without changes.
expected: Styled elements get BEM classes derived from their names, e.g. .hero, .hero__title, .hero__call-to-action; name collisions get a numeric suffix; user classes are kept alongside.
styles.css contains one rule per styled element and no rule for unstyled ones; no selector uses ids or data attributes.
The product name appears in no class and no CSS.
The two ZIPs are byte-identical.

title: Structure elements: Container, Header, Navigation, Main, Section, Article, Aside, Footer, Link Block
steps: Insert each structure element from the Elements panel.
Set the Link Block's link to https://example.com.
Export.
expected: Each element has its default name, default styles and renders as its tag: div, header, nav, main, section, article, aside, footer and a (block link); there is no Card element type.
Empty structure elements keep a visible minimum height on the canvas that is not exported.
The export writes the same tags; the Link Block has the href.

title: Text elements: Heading, Paragraph, Link, Blockquote, Preformatted, Divider
steps: Insert each text element.
Set the Heading level to h3, the Link URL and 'open in a new tab' [inspector.link.openInNewTab].
Type multi-line text with extra spaces in Preformatted.
Export.
expected: Elements render as h1-h6, p, a, blockquote, pre and hr with their default text and styles; there is no Badge element type.
The Link stores href and target=_blank with rel='noopener noreferrer'; unsafe URLs are refused.
Preformatted keeps line breaks and spaces; Divider is a void element with no text.
The export writes the same tags and attributes.

title: List elements: Unordered, Ordered and Definition lists with their items
steps: Insert an Unordered list, an Ordered list and a Definition list from the Elements panel.
Add items by duplicating a list item (Ctrl+D); in the Definition list duplicate the term and the description.
Export.
expected: The Elements panel offers Unordered, Ordered and Definition lists; List item, Term and Description are not palette items.
New lists come with their items so they are never empty: ul and ol with one li, dl with one dt and one dd.
The iframe and the export render ul/ol/li and dl/dt/dd with the texts and default styles.

title: HTML nesting rules for inserting, dragging and pasting
steps: Select an Unordered list and click Paragraph in the Elements panel.
Drag a Paragraph into an Unordered list on the canvas and in Layers.
Copy a List item and paste it into a Section.
Try to put a Link Block inside a Link Block.
expected: Each attempt is refused with a message such as 'Refused. <ul> only accepts <li>' [status.refused.onlyAccepts] and the document JSON is unchanged.
During a drag the refused target shows a refusal indicator and no insertion line.

The rules live in one table covering allowed children (only), required parents (needs), unique children, void elements and no interactive content inside interactive content; a unit test checks the table.
Click insert, canvas drag, Layers drag and paste call the same rule function.

title: HTML nesting rules for wrap, unwrap, promote, tag switch and hand
steps: Select a List item and press R.
Select a List item and press P.
Unwrap an Unordered list that sits in a Section.
Switch the tag of a Section that contains a Main to header (a main may not sit inside a header).
Take a List item into the hand and aim it at the Page.
expected: Each change that would break the nesting rules is refused with a message naming the rule and the document JSON is unchanged.
The hand never offers a target the rules refuse.
Wrap, unwrap, promote, tag switch and hand call the same rule function as insert, drag and paste (unit test with one table of cases run through every path).

title: Table elements: Table, Caption, Head, Body, Footer, Row, Header cell, Cell
steps: Insert a Table from the Elements panel.
In the Table's controls in the Inspector turn on Caption and Footer, then turn Head off and on again.
Edit cell texts.
Export.
expected: The Elements panel offers Table only; Caption, Head, Body, Footer, Row, Header cell and Cell are not palette items.
A new Table comes with a head row of two header cells and a body of two rows of two cells.
The Table's controls add and remove its caption, head and footer; the iframe renders caption, thead, tbody, tfoot, tr, th and td in valid order (caption first).
Only one caption, thead and tfoot are allowed per table.
The export writes the same table markup.

title: Add and remove table rows and columns
steps: Insert a Table with a Head row of two Header cells and a Body with two rows of two Cells, and select a body Cell.
Run 'Add a column after this one' [command.table.addColumnAfter], 'Add a column at the end' [command.table.addColumnEnd] and 'Remove this column' [command.table.removeColumn] from the context menu.
Run 'Add a row after this one' [command.table.addRowAfter] and 'Remove this row' [command.table.removeRow].
expected: Adding a column inserts a cell at the same index in every row (th in head rows, td elsewhere); the status bar reads 'Column created in N rows' [status.table.columnCreated].
Removing a column removes the cell at that index from every row.
Adding a row copies the row's cell structure with empty cells; removing a row removes it.
Each command is one undo step.

title: Form structure elements: Form, Fieldset, Legend, Label, Button, Output
steps: Insert a Form and set action and method.
Insert a Fieldset (it comes with its Legend) and a Label with text.
Insert a Button and set type submit/button/reset; insert an Output.
Insert a Link, switch its tag to button and back to a.
Export.
expected: Elements render as form, fieldset, legend, label, button and output with their attributes.
A new Fieldset comes with its Legend, which is not a palette item; a Fieldset allows one Legend, as its first child.
Switching a Link to a button and back keeps its text and styles; the link URL is kept on the a and not written on the button.
Buttons and form submission do not navigate the editor when clicked on the canvas.
The export writes the same tags and attributes.

title: Custom attributes and accessibility fields
steps: Select a Button and add aria-label, aria-expanded and data-state attributes and a role.
Try to add an onclick attribute and an attribute with an invalid name.
Export.
expected: Custom attributes (aria-*, data-*, role) are stored in the document JSON and rendered in the iframe and the export; they are the user's own, unlike the editor-generated attributes that the export never writes.
on* attributes and invalid attribute names are refused with a message.
Each change is one undo step.

title: Reusable style classes
steps: Style a Button and save its styles as the class 'button-primary'.
Apply the class to two other buttons.
Change the class's background; override the background on one button only.
expected: A class holds styles shared by every element that uses it; editing the class updates all of them.
An element's own values override the class and the inspector shows which values come from the class.
The export writes one rule for the class and element rules only for the overrides.

title: Input elements: the 14 input types and their attributes
steps: Insert each input: Text, Email, Password, Number, Telephone, URL, Search, Date, Time, Color, Range, Checkbox, Radio, File.
Set name, placeholder, value, required, pattern, min, max, step, autocomplete, disabled, readonly and checked where they apply.
Export.
expected: Each input renders with its type in the iframe.
Attributes are stored in the document JSON and rendered in the iframe and the export.

title: Per-type input attributes, type switching, label targets and canvas focus
steps: Select a Checkbox and a Number input and compare their attribute fields.
Change an input's type from text to email and then to checkbox.
Insert a Label and pick an input in its 'for' field.
Click into an input on the canvas and type.
expected: The inspector shows only the attributes valid for the input type (e.g. checked for checkbox and radio; min, max and step for number, range, date and time).
Switching type keeps the attributes that stay valid and drops the others.
A Label's 'for' field offers the ids of the form controls on the page (giving the control an id if it has none) and the exported label points to that id.
Inputs on the canvas never take focus or text while editing; clicking selects the element and typing does not change its value.

title: Textarea, Select, Option group, Option, Progress and Meter
steps: Insert a Textarea and set rows and placeholder.
Insert a Select; in its options editor in the Inspector add an Option group with two Options, set option values and a selected option, reorder and remove an option.
Insert a Progress and a Meter and set value, min and max.
Export.
expected: The Elements panel offers Textarea, Select, Progress and Meter; Option group and Option are not palette items.
A new Select comes with three options; its options editor adds, reorders and removes options and option groups.
Each element renders with its attributes in the iframe.
A Select only accepts option and optgroup; an optgroup only accepts option.
The export writes the same markup and attributes.

title: Image, Picture, Source, Figure and Caption
steps: Insert an Image without a source.
Set its source URL and alt text.
Insert a Picture and add a Source (srcset, media) with the Picture's controls; insert a Figure (it comes with an Image and a Caption).
Export.
expected: Source and Caption are not palette items: a Picture comes with an Image and its controls add, reorder and remove Sources; a Figure comes with an Image and a Caption.
An image without a source shows a placeholder with its size (e.g. '800 x 300') on the canvas.
Source URL and alt are stored in the document JSON; unsafe URLs are refused.
The iframe and the export render img, picture/source and figure/figcaption; an exported image without alt gets alt=''.

title: Video, Audio, Track, Embedded frame and Canvas
steps: Insert a Video; add a Source and a Track with the Video's controls; set controls, autoplay, loop, muted and poster.
Insert an Audio and add a Source with its controls.
Insert an Embedded frame with a URL and title; insert a Canvas with width and height.
Export.
expected: Source and Track are not palette items: Video and Audio add, reorder and remove their Sources and Tracks from their own controls.
Each element renders with its attributes; media do not autoplay inside the editor canvas.
The embedded frame is sandboxed in the editor so it cannot steal pointer events from the canvas.
The export writes video/audio/source/track/iframe/canvas with the attributes.

title: SVG/Icon, Rectangle, Ellipse and Line
steps: Insert an SVG/Icon and add a Rectangle, an Ellipse and a Line with the SVG's controls.
Set fill, stroke and stroke width on the shapes, set one shape's fill from the quick panel's Fill, and size the shapes with the handles.
Paste icon markup (an <svg> with a path) into the SVG's markup field.
Export.
expected: Rectangle, Ellipse and Line are not palette items: they are added inside a selected SVG from its controls and only go inside an SVG; the SVG has a viewBox that matches its size.
Fill, stroke and stroke-width are stored and rendered; the quick panel's Fill writes a shape's fill with the same command as the inspector.
Markup typed or pasted into the SVG's markup field becomes the SVG's content, rendered and exported as written, with scripts and event attributes removed.
The export writes inline <svg> with its shapes and markup.

title: Details, Summary and Dialog
steps: Insert a Details (it comes with its Summary) and add content; toggle its open attribute.
Insert a Dialog with content; toggle its open attribute.
Export.
expected: Summary is not a palette item: a Details always has exactly one Summary as first child.
The open attribute is stored; on the canvas a closed Details still shows its content while it or a descendant is selected.
A closed Dialog is visible on the canvas while selected and exported closed (no open attribute) unless set.
The export writes details/summary and dialog.

title: Create the natural child inside a container
steps: Select an Unordered list and run 'Create <li> inside' [command.createNaturalChild] from the context menu.
Do the same on a Select (option), a Figure without caption (figcaption) and a table body (tr).
Select a Details and open the context menu.
expected: The command label names the child tag for the selected element and appends that child with default content.
It is disabled when the element has no natural child or the child is unique and already present (a Details always has its Summary, so it is disabled there).
Each is one undo step and selects the new child.

title: List, table, form and media properties shown only where they apply
steps: Select an unordered list and set list-style-type, list-style-position and list-style-image.
Select a table and set border-collapse, border-spacing, table-layout, caption-side and empty-cells.
Select a text input and set resize, accent-color, caret-color and appearance.
Select an image and set object-fit and object-position.
expected: Each group appears only for elements of its kind.
Every value is written to the document JSON and the computed style in the iframe matches.

title: Layout templates: Container, Row, Column, Grid
steps: Click each layout template in the Templates group.
Drag the Grid template onto the canvas.
expected: Row inserts a flex row with two columns; Column inserts a flex column with two blocks; Grid inserts a grid with three cells and grid-template-columns repeat(3, minmax(0, 1fr)).
Each template is inserted as one undo step and its root is selected.
Template wrappers use the same layout styles as the wrap commands.

title: Content templates: lists, table, form, select and figure
steps: Click List 3 items, Ordered 3 items, Definition list, Table 2 x 2, Form with fields, Select with options and Figure + caption.
expected: Each inserts a valid subtree: ul with 3 li; ol with 3 li; dl with dt and dd; table with thead (2 th) and tbody (2 rows of 2 td); form with two labelled inputs and a submit button; select with 3 options; figure with image and caption.
Every subtree passes the nesting rules and exports with the same markup.

title: Section templates: Card, Hero, Navbar, Sidebar, Gallery
steps: Click Card, Hero, Navbar, Sidebar and Gallery in the Templates group.
expected: Card inserts an article with image, heading, text and action; Hero a section with heading, supporting line and two buttons; Navbar a header with brand, nav links and a sign-in button; Sidebar an aside with a heading and a list of links; Gallery a section with three figures.

Each template carries default styles in the document JSON (Card: padding, border radius and border; Hero: large heading and generous padding; Navbar: flex row with space-between; Sidebar: fixed width; Gallery: three-column grid) and the export writes them to styles.css without inline styles.

title: Reusable components with instances
steps: Turn a Card into a component and place two more instances.
Edit the component's heading style; override the text of one instance.
Detach one instance.
expected: Instances follow the component's structure and styles; per-instance overrides of text and attributes are kept.
Detaching turns an instance into a normal subtree.
The export writes plain HTML for every instance, with the component's styles written once.

title: Component templates: Form group, Button group, Tabs, Accordion, Modal
steps: Click Form group, Button group, Tabs, Accordion and Modal in the Templates group.
expected: Form group inserts labelled fields; Button group a row of buttons; Tabs a nav of tab buttons and a panel; Accordion two details with summaries; Modal a dialog with heading, content and close button.
Each passes the nesting rules and exports with the same markup.

title: Search the Elements panel and collapse its groups
steps: Type 'inp' in Search elements.
Type 'zzzz'.
Clear the search; collapse the Text group and reload.
expected: Groups are Structure and layout, Text, Lists, Tables, Forms, Images and media, Interactive and Templates, each with its count; internal parts of composite elements (list items, table parts, options and option groups, sources, tracks, captions, legend, summary, SVG shapes) are not listed.
Searching filters by label and tag; 'inp' shows the 14 input types; the footer reads 'N of M elements match' [palette.search.matchCount], where M is the number of entries in the Elements panel.
A search with no match says so.
Collapsed groups stay collapsed after reload.

title: Elements panel view density
steps: Click List view, Two columns, Three columns and Icon grid in the Elements panel.
Reload.
expected: Each density lays items out as described (one per row with tag, two or three per row, icons only with the label as tooltip); measured item sizes change accordingly.
The chosen density is stored in the single preferences store and restored after reload.

title: Collapse and expand every branch in Layers
steps: Insert several nested templates.
Click 'Collapse every branch' [layers.collapseAll], then 'Expand every branch' [layers.expandAll].
Collapse all, then select a deeply nested element on the canvas.
expected: Collapse all leaves only top-level rows visible; expand all shows every row.
Selecting a hidden descendant expands its ancestors and scrolls its row into view.

title: Search the Layers panel
steps: Insert the Card and Navbar templates.
Type 'card' in Search layers.
Clear the search.
expected: Only rows whose name, tag, id or class matches are shown, with their ancestors for context and the match highlighted.
Clicking a result selects the element.
Clearing restores the previous expansion state.

title: Choose what each Layers row shows
steps: Open 'What each row shows' [layers.rowDetails] in the Layers toolbar.
Turn on ID, Classes and Attributes; turn off HTML tag.
Reload.
expected: Rows show the chosen details (name, HTML tag, id, classes, attributes) next to the name.
The choice is stored in the preferences store and restored after reload.

title: Colour labels on Layers rows
steps: Click the colour dot of a Section row and choose a colour.
Select the Section on the canvas.
Reload.
expected: The colour dot opens a small palette; the chosen colour tints the row and is stored in the page settings of the document JSON.
The canvas selection outline of that element uses its label colour.
The colour is restored after reload and never exported.

title: Zoom with the keyboard, the status bar buttons and Fit
steps: Press Ctrl+= three times, Ctrl+- once, Ctrl+0.
Click the zoom-in and zoom-out buttons and the zoom percentage.
Click Fit.
expected: Ctrl+= and Ctrl+- change zoom by 10 points, Ctrl+0 sets 100%; the iframe CSS zoom and the percentage in the status bar match.
Zoom stays between 10% and 800%; the page point at the centre of the canvas stays under the centre.
Clicking the percentage opens a menu with 25%, 50%, 100%, 200%, 400% and Fit.
Fit sets the zoom so the whole page width fits in the canvas and keeps it fitted when the canvas size changes; any manual zoom leaves Fit mode until Fit is chosen again.
The zoom (or Fit mode) is restored after a reload.

title: Rotate an element with a handle on the canvas
steps: Select a Container.
Drag its rotation handle a quarter turn clockwise; repeat with Shift held.
Type 30 in the inspector's Rotate field.
Zoom to 200% and rotate again with the handle.
expected: A rotation handle sits outside the selection outline at a fixed screen distance; over it the cursor shows rotation.
Dragging rotates around the transform-origin and the angle follows the pointer; Shift snaps to 15° steps; the status bar shows the live angle.
The handle and the Rotate field run the same command and write the rotate part of the one transform value; a whole drag is one undo step.
The angle does not depend on the zoom; the outline and handles follow the rotated box.

title: Ctrl+wheel zoom, wheel scroll and Space-drag pan
steps: Place the pointer over a heading and scroll the wheel with Ctrl held.
Scroll the wheel without modifiers, then with Shift.
Hold Space and drag the canvas.
expected: Ctrl+wheel zooms around the pointer: the heading stays under the pointer.
Wheel scrolls vertically and Shift+wheel horizontally; the page can be scrolled to see content below the fold.
Holding Space shows a grab cursor and dragging pans the view without selecting or moving anything; releasing Space returns to selection.

title: Rulers along the canvas
steps: Look at the top and left rulers; zoom in and scroll.
Select an element.
Move the pointer over the page.
expected: The rulers fill the 20 px bands reserved along the top and left of the canvas; the canvas viewport and the page position do not move.
