The rulers show page CSS px with 0 at the page top-left; labelled ticks sit on round values (10, 25, 50, 100, 250, 500...) chosen so neighbouring labels are at least 40 screen px apart at any zoom.
They update with zoom and scroll.
The selected element's extent is highlighted on both rulers and a marker follows the pointer position.

title: Create, move and delete guides from the rulers
steps: Drag from the top ruler down onto the page and release.
Drag from the left ruler onto the page and release.
Drag the horizontal guide to a new position.
Drag the vertical guide back onto its ruler.
Reload.
expected: Dragging out of the top ruler creates a horizontal guide and out of the left ruler a vertical guide, each labelled with its position in page px.
Guides can be moved; dropping a guide on its ruler deletes it.
Guides are stored per page in the document JSON, restored after reload and never exported; creating, moving and deleting guides are undo steps.

title: Show element outlines and drop zones on the canvas
steps: Open Canvas tools and turn on Outlines.
Turn on Zones.
Turn both off.
expected: Outlines draw a dashed box around every element on the canvas.
Zones show the padding and empty drop areas of containers.
Neither changes the document JSON or the export; the choices are stored in preferences.

title: Column grid, row grid and dot grid overlays
steps: Press Ctrl+'.
Press Ctrl+' again.
Turn on the row grid and the dot grid from the canvas tools.
expected: Ctrl+' toggles a 12-column grid overlay (1280 px wide, 24 px gutter, 80 px margin by default) drawn over the page at the right page coordinates.
The row grid draws horizontal bands and the dot grid draws dots, each at its default spacing.
Grid settings are stored per page in the document JSON and never exported.

title: Guides & Grids settings dialog
steps: Open View > Guides & Grids.
Turn rulers and manual guides off and on.
Add a vertical guide at 400 by typing it.
Set the column grid to 6 columns, 960 width, 16 gutter, 40 margin; set row height and row gutter; set the dot spacing.
Close the dialog with Escape.
expected: The dialog has Visibility, Manual guides, Column grid, Row grid and Dot grid sections, each with an info tooltip.
Each change applies to the canvas immediately and is stored (visibility in preferences, grids and guides in the page).
Escape and the close button close the dialog and return focus to where it was.

title: Free positioning of absolute children by dragging
steps: Insert a Section with a Heading; set the Heading position to absolute.
Drag the Heading 60 px right and 40 px down on the canvas.
expected: Setting absolute on a child of a static parent sets the parent to position relative and keeps the child's visual position (top/left computed from its old place).
Dragging an absolute child moves it freely; the status bar shows its coordinates relative to the parent; release writes top and left to the document JSON.
The measured position in the iframe equals the stored top and left.

title: Nudge positioned elements with the arrow keys
steps: Select an absolutely positioned element on the canvas.
Press ArrowRight, Shift+ArrowDown, ArrowLeft three times quickly.
expected: For a selection that is absolutely or fixed positioned, arrows move the element by 1 px and Shift+arrows by 10 px instead of walking the tree; top/left in the document JSON change accordingly.
The status bar reads 'Moved to x, y' [status.movedTo].
A quick burst of nudges is one undo step.

title: Anchor positioned elements to edges and centres
steps: Select an absolutely positioned element.
Press Alt+Shift+ArrowRight, Alt+Shift+ArrowDown.
Use the anchor control in the inspector to anchor horizontally to the centre.
Resize the parent.
expected: Alt+Shift+arrow toggles the anchor on that edge; anchoring both left and right stores left and right (width follows the parent).
Anchoring the centre stores left:50% with a translate so the element stays centred.
Toggling an anchor never moves the element visually; after resizing the parent the element keeps its distances to the anchored edges.

title: Align and distribute positioned elements
steps: Place three absolutely positioned boxes in a positioned Container and select them.
Run Align left, Align centre and Align top; then Distribute horizontally.
Select one box and run Align centre.
expected: With several elements selected, align works on the selection's bounds; with one element, on its parent's box.
Distribute makes the gaps between the elements equal.
The commands are in the quick panel and the Arrange menu; top and left are written for each element as one undo step, and the measured positions in the iframe match.

title: Snap on/off and snap settings
steps: Click 'Snap: Off' [topbar.snap.off] in the top bar.
Open the snap menu and choose Snap settings.
Untick Grid and Centers, set snap distance 10 and Apply; reopen and Cancel after changes.
expected: The top bar button toggles between 'Snap: Off' [topbar.snap.off] and 'Snap: On' [topbar.snap.on].
Snap settings lists Page, Parent, Elements, Guides, Rulers, Grid, Centers and Edges targets and a snap distance in px.
Apply stores the settings in preferences; Cancel discards changes.

title: Snapping while resizing and moving positioned elements
steps: Turn snap on and add a vertical guide at x=400.
Resize a Container so its right edge passes near the guide.
Drag an absolutely positioned element so its left edge passes near another element's left edge and near the page centre.
Repeat holding Alt.
expected: Within the snap distance the edge jumps to the target and a snap line is drawn; the stored value is exactly the target position.
Only enabled targets snap.
Holding Alt suspends snapping for that gesture.

title: Smart alignment and equal spacing guides
steps: Place three absolutely positioned boxes in a positioned container.
Drag one box so it aligns with the centre of another, then so the gaps between the three become equal.
In View > Guides & Grids turn Smart guides off and repeat.
expected: Alignment lines appear when edges or centres align with other elements.
Equal spacing markers appear when the gaps are equal and the box snaps to the equal-gap position when snap is on, using the snap distance from Snap settings (one setting).
The Guides & Grids dialog gains a Smart guides toggle under Visibility and an Equal spacing toggle; turning smart guides off removes these hints.

title: Measure sizes and distances on the canvas
steps: Hover an element with nothing selected.
Select a Container, hold Alt and hover a sibling.
Hold Alt and hover the selection's parent.
Zoom to 50% and repeat.
expected: Hovering shows the element's size (W × H in CSS px) next to its hover outline.

With a selection, holding Alt over another element draws distance lines between the nearest edges, each labelled in CSS px; over an ancestor it shows the distances from the selection to the ancestor's inner edges.
The values are CSS px at any zoom and equal the measured geometry in the iframe.
Measuring never changes the selection or the document JSON.

title: Switch between Desktop, Laptop, Tablet and Phone breakpoints
steps: Click Laptop, Tablet, Phone and Desktop in the top bar.
expected: The page width inside the iframe becomes 1180 CSS px for Laptop, 834 for Tablet, 390 for Phone and 1440 for Desktop; in Fit mode the canvas refits the zoom.
The status bar shows the active breakpoint; the buttons show their widths in tooltips.
The breakpoint buttons and the canvas widths read one breakpoint table (a unit test checks it).
The active breakpoint is restored after a reload.

title: Style overrides per breakpoint, desktop first
steps: Select a Heading at Desktop with font size 32px.
Switch to Tablet and set font size 24px; switch to Phone and look at it.
Switch to Desktop and Laptop.
At Tablet reset the override.
Export.
expected: The Tablet value is stored as an override for tablet in the document JSON; at Tablet and Phone the computed font size is 24px, at Desktop and Laptop 32px.
Fields with an override at the active breakpoint show a badge naming the breakpoint; inherited values show where they come from.
Resetting the override returns Tablet and Phone to 32px.
styles.css contains the base rule and @media (max-width: 834px) with the override, in cascade order.
The export media queries read the same breakpoint table as the buttons and the canvas (unit test).

title: Style states: hover, focus, active, disabled, invalid and placeholder shown
steps: Select a Button, choose State Hover and set background colour and opacity.
Choose Focus and set an outline; choose Base.
Switch to Tablet and set a Hover value there.
Export.
expected: The State menu lists Base, Hover, Focus, Active, Disabled, Invalid and Placeholder shown; while a state is chosen a canvas badge reads 'Editing Hover' [canvas.badge.editingState] and the canvas shows the element with that state's values.
State values are stored per state (and per breakpoint) in the document JSON and do not change the base values.
styles.css contains :hover, :focus and @media rules for them; in the exported page hovering the button changes its computed background.

title: Preview the page without editor chrome
steps: Build a page with a Button that has a hover state and a Details element.
Press Ctrl+P (or click Preview).
Hover the button, open the details, switch to Phone.
Press Escape.
expected: Preview hides docks, selection, guides and handles; only a slim bar with the breakpoint switcher, Exit preview and Export remains.
The page renders exactly like the export: hover states apply and details open; links do not navigate the editor away.
Escape or Ctrl+Enter exits preview and restores the previous selection and zoom.
Preview never changes the document JSON.

title: Embed custom HTML
steps: Insert an Embed and paste third-party widget markup with a script.
Preview the page.
Export.
expected: The markup is stored as-is and shown sandboxed on the editing canvas, where its scripts never run.
Preview runs it.
The export writes it verbatim at its place; Layers marks it as an embed.

title: Light, dark and system theme
steps: Choose Theme > Light, then Dark, then System.
With System chosen, switch the OS/browser colour scheme emulation.
Reload.
expected: The editor chrome switches its colour tokens; the page inside the iframe keeps its own colours.
System follows prefers-color-scheme live.
The choice is stored in the preferences store and restored after reload.

title: Show and hide the docks and panels
steps: Press Ctrl+B twice; press Ctrl+Alt+B twice.
Press Ctrl+\ twice.
Close the Layers panel with its close button and reopen it from the top bar and from View.
expected: Ctrl+B hides and shows the left dock; Ctrl+Alt+B hides and shows the inspector; the canvas grows into the freed space and refits in Fit mode. While editing text Ctrl+B keeps its bold meaning.
Ctrl+\ collapses every dock and the second press restores exactly what was open.
Panels close and reopen from the top bar toggles and the View menu; the status bar reports each change.

title: Command bar with Ctrl+K
steps: Press Ctrl+K.
Type 'wrap' and press Enter.
Press Ctrl+K, type 'insert hero', use ArrowDown and Enter.
Press Ctrl+K, type 'layers' and press Enter; press Ctrl+K and Escape.
expected: The command bar lists commands, panels ('Open Layers' [command.openPanel]) and element types ('Insert Hero' [command.insertElement]), each with its shortcut where it has one; fuzzy search filters them.
ArrowUp/ArrowDown move the highlight, Enter runs it and closes the bar; Escape and clicking outside close it.
Commands that cannot apply to the current selection are not offered.
Recently run commands are listed first.
While editing text Ctrl+K keeps its link meaning and does not open the bar.

title: Set a property or jump to it from the command bar
steps: Select a flex Container, press Ctrl+K, type 'gap 24' and press Enter.
Press Ctrl+K, type 'width 50%' and press Enter.
Press Ctrl+K, type 'border-color' and choose 'Edit property border-color' [command.editProperty].
expected: Typing '<property> <value>' offers 'Set <property> to <value>' [command.setProperty]; running it writes the value to the selection in the document JSON as one undo step.
Invalid values are not offered.
'Edit property X' [command.editProperty] opens the section, reveals the field in the inspector and focuses it.

title: Keyboard shortcuts panel generated from the keymap
steps: Open Help > Keyboard shortcuts.
expected: The shortcuts open as a tab in the bottom workbench dock; the workbench is closed by default and opens with its first tab.
The panel lists every binding grouped by context (anywhere, on the canvas, while editing text, during a drag, with something in hand, on panels) with keys and a description.
It is rendered from the single keymap table: a unit test adds a binding to the table and the panel shows it without other changes.

title: Bottom workbench: tabs, collapse, maximise and developer tools
steps: Open the Keyboard shortcuts tab; turn on View > Developer tools and switch between the Keyboard shortcuts and Document tabs.
Click 'Show or hide the workbench' [workbench.toggle], then 'Maximize the workbench' [workbench.maximize] and restore it.
Make a change on the canvas; close the Document tab.
expected: The workbench shows one tab strip; the chosen tab's content fills it; tabs can be closed.
It collapses to its tab strip, expands, and maximises to cover the canvas area, then restores.
Developer tools adds a Document tab showing the live document JSON read-only, updated after every command; the choice is stored in preferences.

title: Resize docks and panels with splitters
steps: Drag the splitter between the left dock and the canvas; drag the splitter between Elements and Layers.
Drag the inspector splitter; drag the workbench splitter.
Focus a splitter and press ArrowLeft and ArrowRight.
Reload.
expected: Each splitter resizes its neighbours with the mouse and by 20 px per arrow key, within minimum and maximum sizes.
Splitters have role separator with aria-valuenow.
Sizes are restored after reload.

title: Float a panel as a window and dock it again
steps: Drag the Layers panel header onto the canvas and release.
Drag the floating window around; close it and reopen it.
Drag it to the right edge of the window and release; drag it to the left edge and release.
Start dragging a panel and press Escape.
expected: A panel dragged out of its dock becomes a floating window at the drop point, kept inside the viewport.
Near the left or right edge a 'Dock left' [workspace.hint.dockLeft]/'Dock right' [workspace.hint.dockRight] hint appears and release docks the panel there.
Escape cancels the drag and returns the panel where it was.
The floating layout is restored after reload.

title: Combine panels as tabs or stack them
steps: Drag the Layers panel over the upper part of the Elements panel and release.
Switch between the two tabs.
Drag the Layers tab over the lower part of the Elements panel and release.
expected: Over the upper part a 'Combine as tabs' [workspace.hint.combineTabs] hint appears and release shows both panels as tabs of one panel.
Over the lower part a 'Stack panels' [workspace.hint.stackPanels] hint appears and release stacks them vertically.
The arrangement is restored after reload.

title: Workspace layout persists and can be reset
steps: Hide the inspector, resize the left dock, float the Layers panel and collapse an inspector section.
Reload.
Choose View > Reset workspace.
expected: After reload the workspace looks exactly as it was left.
Reset workspace restores the default docks, sizes and panels and says so in the status bar; the document JSON is untouched.

title: Status bar: messages, breadcrumb, size, context, count, zoom and save state
steps: Select a nested element; click an ancestor in the breadcrumb.
Run a few commands, change breakpoint and state.
expected: The status bar shows the last message (in an aria-live region), the breadcrumb of the selection, its W x H, the breakpoint and state, the node count, the zoom and the save state.
Clicking a breadcrumb ancestor selects it.
Every value updates immediately after each command.

title: Accessibility and structure checks
steps: Build a page with an image without alt, a skipped heading level, low-contrast text and a link without text.
Open the Checks panel and click each issue.
expected: Each issue is listed with its rule, the element and a suggested fix; clicking it selects the element on the canvas and in Layers.
The list updates after every command.
Checks never block editing or export.

title: Move between panels and inside them with the keyboard
steps: Press F6 repeatedly, then Shift+F6.
In a tab strip press ArrowRight, Home, End and Enter.
In the top bar toolbar press ArrowRight and ArrowLeft.
Press Escape inside a panel.
expected: F6 and Shift+F6 cycle focus between top bar, left dock, canvas, inspector, workbench and status bar; the focused region shows a visible focus ring.
Tab strips and toolbars use roving tabindex: arrows move, Home/End jump, Enter/Space activate.
Escape inside a panel returns focus to the canvas with the selection intact.
An automated sweep that presses F6 and Tab through the whole UI reaches every enabled button, input, tab and tree of every open panel.

title: Operate the Layers tree with the keyboard
steps: Focus the Layers tree.
Press ArrowDown, ArrowUp, ArrowRight on a collapsed row, ArrowLeft on an expanded row, Home, End.
Press Enter, F2, Delete and Alt+ArrowUp on a row.
expected: The tree has role tree with treeitems, aria-level and aria-expanded; one row is focusable at a time.
Arrows move focus and expand/collapse as in the WAI-ARIA tree pattern; Home/End jump to first/last visible row.
Enter selects the element, F2 renames, Delete deletes and Alt+ArrowUp moves it, with the same commands as the canvas.

title: Cut, and copy elements as HTML for other applications
steps: Insert the Card template, select its root and press Ctrl+X.
Select a Section and press Ctrl+V.
Press Ctrl+C on the pasted Card and read the system clipboard's text/html.
expected: Ctrl+X copies the element to the system clipboard and deletes it as one undo step; Cut appears in the context menu and the Edit menu.
Copy also writes text/html of the element's exported markup with its CSS rules, next to the app's element format.
The clipboard text/html contains no editor attributes, editor-generated ids or inline styles.

title: Copy and paste styles between elements
steps: Select a styled Heading and press Ctrl+Alt+C.
Select a Paragraph and press Ctrl+Alt+V.
Press Ctrl+Z.
expected: Copy style puts every style value of the element on the system clipboard in the app format.
Paste style replaces the target's style values with the copied ones as one undo step; text, children and attributes stay.
Both commands are in the context menu and the Edit menu with their shortcuts.

title: Import an HTML file: tags, text, inline marks and attributes
steps: Choose File > Import HTML and pick an .html file with headings, paragraphs with strong/em/a, lists, a table, a form, images and links.
Confirm replacing the page.
expected: Each supported tag becomes the matching element type in the document JSON with its text, inline marks and supported attributes (href, src, alt, type, name, ...).
Element names are taken from BEM classes when present, else from the element type.
The import is one undo step.

title: Import cleaning: scripts, unknown elements, broken nesting and the import report
steps: Import an HTML file that contains an inline
expected: Scripts are not dropped: each is kept with its page (its code or its src), never run on the editing canvas, written back by the export, and listed in the report; event handler attributes are removed and listed in the report.
Unknown elements are unwrapped into their children.
Structures that break the nesting rules are repaired (e.g. a stray li gets a ul) or dropped; the resulting document always passes the nesting rules.
An import report lists everything that was dropped, unwrapped, repaired or kept, with the source line.

title: Import CSS: style attributes, style blocks and linked stylesheets
steps: Choose File > Import HTML and pick, in one selection, an HTML file and the stylesheet it links; the page also has a <style> block with class, tag and id rules and style attributes (a fixture whose rules are all mappable).
Import the same page again without its stylesheet.
expected: The import accepts several files at once; a linked stylesheet is found by its path among the picked files.
Declarations that apply to each element, resolved by specificity and order, become that element styles in the document JSON.
For this fixture, the computed styles of every element in the iframe match the original file opened in Chrome.
A linked stylesheet that was not picked is listed in the import report.

title: Import @media rules as breakpoint overrides
steps: Import an HTML file whose CSS has @media (max-width: 834px) and @media (max-width: 390px) rules, and a @media (min-width: 1000px) rule.
expected: max-width rules at a breakpoint width become overrides of that breakpoint; other widths map to the nearest breakpoint at or below them and are reported.
Rules that cannot be mapped (min-width, orientation, print) are listed in the import report.
At each breakpoint the computed styles in the iframe match the original page at that width for every element not affected by a reported rule.

title: Import pseudo-class rules as state styles
steps: Import an HTML file whose CSS has :hover, :focus, :active, :disabled, :invalid and :placeholder-shown rules, plus a descendant selector and an @supports block.
expected: Each supported pseudo-class rule becomes a state style of the matching element in the document JSON.
Selectors that cannot be mapped to single elements (descendant rules across unrelated elements, @supports, ::before) are listed in the import report.
In preview, hovering an imported element shows its hover styles.

title: Exported pages import back unchanged
steps: Build a page using templates, breakpoint overrides and hover states and export it.
Choose File > Import HTML and pick the exported ZIP.
Export again.
expected: Importing a ZIP imports its pages together with their linked CSS files as a whole.

The imported document equals the original in tag structure, texts, attributes and styles per breakpoint and state; element types are compared by HTML tag (types that share a tag, such as Link and Link Block, cannot be told apart in plain HTML); ids and editor-only data (locks, layer colours, guides, grid settings, saved colours) are ignored.
Element names are recovered from their BEM classes, so the second export is byte-identical to the first.

title: Paste HTML and text copied from outside the app
steps: Put text/html of a small article (heading, paragraphs, a list, a script tag) on the system clipboard and press Ctrl+V with a Section selected.
Put multi-line text/plain on the system clipboard and press Ctrl+V with a Section selected.
expected: Pasted HTML goes through the HTML importer (same cleaning and nesting rules) and is inserted into the selection as one undo step; scripts in pasted HTML are not kept, because a pasted fragment has no page to keep them with.
Plain text becomes one Paragraph per line.
Anything the importer drops is reported in the status bar.

title: Code panel shows the generated HTML and CSS
steps: Open the Code panel.
Switch between the HTML and CSS tabs.
Change a style and insert an element.
expected: View > Code opens the Code panel as a tab in the bottom workbench.
The panel shows index.html and styles.css with line numbers and syntax colouring, identical to the files the export writes.
It updates after every command.
It can be resized and floated like other panels.

title: Code panel follows the selection
steps: Open the Code panel and select an element on the canvas.
Click a line inside another element's markup in the HTML tab.
expected: Selecting an element highlights its markup lines in HTML and its rules in CSS and scrolls them into view.
Clicking inside an element's markup selects that element on the canvas and in Layers.

title: Copy or download what the Code panel shows
steps: In the Code panel click 'Copy this pane' [codePanel.copyPane].
Click 'Download this pane' [codePanel.downloadPane].
expected: The clipboard receives exactly the text of the open tab.
The download is the open file (index.html or styles.css) with exactly the shown content.

title: Edit an element's CSS in the Code panel
steps: Select a Heading and open the CSS tab.
Edit its rule: change a value, add a declaration, remove one, then apply.
Type invalid CSS and apply.
expected: Applying replaces the element's styles in the document JSON with the declarations of its rule as one undo step; the inspector and canvas update.
Invalid CSS is refused with the line and reason, and the document JSON is unchanged.
The rule is edited for the active breakpoint and state.

title: Edit HTML in the Code panel
steps: Select a Section and open the HTML tab.
Edit its markup: change a text, add a paragraph, change an attribute; apply.
Type markup that breaks the nesting rules (an li outside a list) and apply; type unparsable markup and apply.
expected: Applying parses the markup with the HTML importer's rules and replaces the element's subtree in the document JSON as one undo step; the canvas, Layers and the inspector update.
Unchanged nodes keep their ids, names and styles.
Markup that breaks the nesting rules or cannot be parsed is refused with the line and the reason, and the document JSON is unchanged.

title: Timeline panel: create animations for an element
steps: Select a Heading and open the Timeline panel.
Click 'New animation' [timeline.newAnimation], name it 'fade-in'.
Create a second animation and rename and delete it.
expected: View > Timeline opens the Timeline panel as a tab in the bottom workbench.
The Timeline panel lists the animations of the selected element with a time ruler.
New animations are stored in the document JSON with a unique keyframes name, a 1 s duration and keyframes at 0% and 100%.
Rename and delete are undo steps; a deleted animation leaves no animation properties on the element.

title: Add, edit, move and delete keyframes on the timeline
steps: Select the 'fade-in' animation, move the playhead to 50% and click 'Add keyframe' [timeline.addKeyframe].
With the playhead on the 0% keyframe set opacity 0 and Move Y 20px in the inspector; on 100% set opacity 1 and Move Y 0.
Drag the 50% keyframe to 30%; set its easing to ease-out; delete it.
expected: Keyframes show as diamonds on the track at their percentage.
While the playhead sits on a keyframe the inspector edits that keyframe's values (a badge says so) and not the base styles.
Keyframe offsets, values and per-keyframe easing are stored in the document JSON; moving and deleting are undo steps.

title: Animation duration, delay, repeat, direction and fill
steps: Set duration 800 ms, delay 200 ms, iteration count infinite, direction alternate, fill mode both, timing function ease-in-out and play state paused, then running.
expected: Each setting is stored with the animation in the document JSON.
The animation has no trigger setting of its own.

title: Preview animations by playing and scrubbing the timeline
steps: Click Play on the 'fade-in' animation, then Pause, then Stop.
Drag the playhead from 0% to 100%.
Turn on Loop and play.
expected: Play animates the element on the canvas using the stored keyframes; Pause freezes it; Stop returns it to its base styles.
Scrubbing shows the interpolated state at the playhead: at 50% of a linear 0-to-1 opacity animation the computed opacity is 0.5.
Previewing never changes the document JSON.

title: Export animations as @keyframes
steps: Build an element with the 'fade-in' animation and settings, and export.
expected: styles.css contains @keyframes fade-in with every keyframe and its values, and the animation properties on the element's base rule, so the animation plays when the page loads.
A @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block turns the animations off; it is written only when the page has animations, so pages without animations export exactly as before.
In the exported page the element's computed animation-name is fade-in and two exports are byte-identical.

title: Events and actions per element
steps: Select a Button, open the Interactions section and add: on click, toggle the class 'is-open' on a Container.

Add: on hover, show a hidden element; on scroll into view, play the 'fade-in' animation; on page load, scroll to an element; on submit of a Form, hide the form and show a message; on click, open a link in a new tab.
Remove an action and undo.
expected: Triggers are click, hover (enter and leave), scroll into view, page load and form submit; actions are show, hide, toggle class, play animation, scroll to and open link.
Targets are picked from the page or Layers, never typed ids; combinations that cannot apply (form submit on a non-form) are not offered.
Interactions are stored per element in the document JSON; each add, edit and remove is one undo step.
The editing canvas never runs them.

title: Export interactions as standard JavaScript
steps: Build the interactions of events-actions, preview the page and trigger each event, then export.
expected: The ZIP contains the plain JavaScript file js/interactions.js (no framework, no inline handlers), linked with <script defer> from every page that uses interactions.
Targets are addressed by their BEM class or user id, never by editor ids or data attributes.
An animation played by an event gets a class rule in styles.css, next to its @keyframes, that the script adds when the event fires.
Preview runs every interaction exactly like the exported page; an animation used by a play-animation action no longer plays on page load and plays when its event fires.
In the exported page opened in Chrome every trigger performs its action, checked by class, computed style or scroll position.
Pages without interactions export exactly as before, with no script.

title: File explorer: add, rename, duplicate, delete and switch pages
steps: Open the Explorer panel.
Add a page 'About', rename it 'About us', duplicate it, delete the duplicate after confirming.
Switch between the pages; undo the delete.
expected: View > Explorer opens the Explorer as a tab next to Elements in the left dock; Elements stays the default tab.
The Explorer lists the project pages as .html files; the active page is highlighted and shown on the canvas.

Each page has its own document tree, guides and settings in the project JSON; page names are unique; each page is an .html file whose path follows its name: the home page is index.html and the others take their file name from their name (about-us.html).
The home page cannot be deleted; delete asks for confirmation; every page operation is an undo step.
File > New blank page now empties only the active page; File > Open project replaces all pages.
The active page is restored after reload.

title: File explorer with a virtual file system
steps: Open the Explorer.
Create the folders 'js' and 'img/icons' and the file 'js/main.js'.
Rename a folder; drag a file into another folder; delete a folder that holds files, after confirming.
Click css/styles.css and a page file in the tree.
Undo the delete; reload.
expected: The Explorer shows the project's file tree (pages, CSS, JS, images, fonts) with folders: one .html per page, css/styles.css, js/interactions.js when the project has interactions, and every file the project holds.
Files and folders can be created, renamed, moved (drag and drop, and a Move to… command) and deleted; names are unique per folder.

css/styles.css and js/interactions.js are generated from the document and keep fixed paths: they cannot be renamed, moved or deleted, neither can a folder that holds one of them, and creating or moving another file to either path is refused, even before js/interactions.js exists.

Pages can be moved into folders; a page file is deleted by deleting its page, and a folder that holds a page file cannot be deleted; renaming a page file renames its page and moving it moves the page; a page stores its file name, so a renamed or imported file keeps its exact name (Contact Us.html stays Contact Us.html) while a new page still gets a file name derived from its name (about-us.html); page names are unique within each folder, and pages in different folders may share a name (about/index.html and blog/index.html); the home page's index.html cannot be renamed or moved out of the root.
Deleting a folder that holds files asks for confirmation; every operation is one undo step.
Clicking a page file or css/styles.css opens it in the Code panel; the tree updates when pages or files change.

The tree is stored with the project in IndexedDB and restored after reload; File > Save project and Open project include every file of the tree, and an archive saved in the earlier format (before pages and the file tree) opens and is migrated to the current format; the autosaved project and its saved versions from that format are migrated the same way when the app loads them.

title: Link to pages, anchors, email and phone
steps: Select a Link and pick another page as its target.
Pick an element of the current page as an anchor target.
Enter an email address and a phone number as targets.
Rename and move the target page.
expected: The picker offers the pages of the file tree, the elements of a page (giving them an id if they have none), a URL, email (mailto:) and phone (tel:); unsafe URLs are refused.
Page links are stored as references to the page file.
Renaming or moving the target page updates every link to it.

title: Export every page of the project
steps: Create a project with pages Home and About us, move About us into a folder 'company', link from Home to About us with the link picker, and export.
expected: The ZIP contains index.html, company/about-us.html and one shared css/styles.css, each at its path in the file tree.
Links chosen with the link picker are written as relative links computed from the two files' paths (company/about-us.html from index.html, ../index.html back).
Each page file has its own title, lang and dir, and links the shared stylesheet with a path relative to its folder.

title: Upload and manage image and font files
steps: In the Explorer upload two images and a font file with the file picker.
Drop a third image file onto a folder in the Explorer (the test dispatches a drop whose DataTransfer holds the file).
Rename a file; delete a file.
expected: Uploaded files are ordinary files of the file tree, stored in IndexedDB, placed in the folder they were uploaded or dropped into (img/ by default for images, fonts/ for fonts), and listed with a thumbnail for images, their name and size.
Renaming changes the listed name; names stay unique per folder.
Deleting an unused file removes it from the tree and from IndexedDB, as an undo step.

title: Use assets in Image elements and drop images onto the canvas
steps: Select an Image and choose an uploaded asset with the asset picker of its Source field.
Drop an image file onto the canvas between two elements (the test dispatches a drop whose DataTransfer holds the file).
Rename an asset that is in use; try to delete it.
expected: The Image stores a reference to the asset in the document JSON and renders it on the canvas.
Dropping an image file on the canvas uploads it as an asset and inserts an Image that uses it at the drop position, as one undo step.
Renaming an asset keeps every Image that uses it working.
Deleting an asset in use, or a folder that holds one, asks for confirmation and lists where it is used.

title: Export the file tree as a ZIP
steps: Create folders and files in the Explorer, including a page inside a folder and an image used by it, and export.
expected: The ZIP holds exactly the Explorer's tree: every folder and file at its path, pages generated from the document, CSS in separate files with BEM classes.
Relative links between pages and to files (stylesheets, scripts, images) are computed from their paths, so they follow a moved or renamed file.
Two exports without changes are byte-identical.

title: Export includes every file of the tree
steps: Use two uploaded images in Images, leave a third image unused in its folder, and export.
expected: The ZIP contains every file of the tree at its path, byte-identical to the uploads, the unused image included.
The img src attributes are relative paths to those files and the exported page shows the images.

title: Page metadata for search and sharing
steps: Open Page properties and set the description, the canonical URL, the Open Graph title and image, and the favicon.
Export.
expected: The values are stored in the page settings of the document JSON; image fields pick files from the file tree.
The exported page head has meta description, link rel=canonical, the og: tags and link rel=icon with paths relative to the page file.

title: Use custom font files
steps: Add two .woff2 font files to the project.
Select a Heading and choose the new font in the font menu.
Export.
expected: The font menu lists the project fonts above the system stacks, each previewed in its own face.
The canvas renders the Heading with the font.
The export writes @font-face rules in the CSS pointing to the font files at their paths in the tree, and the exported page renders with the font.

title: Open a whole folder from disk
steps: Choose File > Open folder and pick a folder with index.html, about/index.html, css/site.css, js/app.js and img/logo.png.
Confirm replacing the project.
Export.
expected: The folder is read with Chrome's directory picker and every file lands at the same path in the virtual file system, except a file whose path belongs to a generated file (css/styles.css, js/interactions.js): it is kept under a new name (css/styles-1.css) and the import report lists it.

HTML pages go through the HTML importer with their linked CSS resolved from the folder; each becomes a page named after its file, at its path (about/index.html is the page index in the folder about), and the root index.html is the home page (a folder without one gets an empty home page index.html, listed in the report); CSS, JS, images and fonts are kept as files.
The import report lists what was converted, kept as-is or dropped.
The export right after reproduces the same folder structure.

title: Edit JavaScript files in the Code panel
steps: Create js/main.js in the Explorer, open it in the Code panel, type code and save.
Type a syntax error and save.
Link the script to the page in Page properties and open Preview.
expected: JS files open with line numbers and syntax colouring; saving writes the file in the file tree as one undo step; js/interactions.js, which is generated, opens read-only.
Syntax errors are shown with the line and the reason.
Preview runs the linked scripts and reloads after each save; the editing canvas never runs them.
The export writes the files unchanged and links them from their pages.
Deleting a JS file that a page links, or a folder that holds one, asks for confirmation and lists those pages.

title: Every listed shortcut works in its context
steps: Run the shortcut sweep test: for each row of the keymap, set up its context and press its keys.
expected: Every binding listed in the Keyboard shortcuts panel runs its command in its context, checked by the document JSON, the selection or the UI state it changes.

No two bindings in the same context use the same keys (unit test on the keymap); a context includes what is selected or focused, so the arrow keys nudge a positioned selection and walk the tree otherwise, and keys handled inside a tree, tab strip, splitter or field belong to that control.
Each keymap row declares its own context setup and check next to its binding, so rows added by any entry are swept without editing the sweep test.
